answer: Because the atlas commitment is timestamped in the tundra ledger, the anchor audit verifies the pair and a late swap fails the hash. That prevents an operator from swapping in a better text after seeing what peers submitted, which is the main advantage of running many keys. The answer is committed as a 193 bit hash at open and revealed at close, and a reveal that does not match the commitment is void. Bonded capital sits idle for 5 days. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
